messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problems with prediction of a spatial model
parts:
Hi,
Check if it's simply an effect of the nonlinear transformation.
Since E( exp(X) ) > exp( E(X) ), just taking the transformation of the posterior mean of the linear predictor does not give the posterior mean of the transformed prediction.  Fitted values calculates E(exp(X)), but it looks like your code calculates exp(E(X)).

Finn

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problems with prediction of a spatial model
parts:
You have to take into account that the Region.un is 61 for the first
line of the dataset. So the correct computed by hand would be

exp(result1$summary.fixed[1,1] +
result1$summary.ran$region$mean[61] +
result1$summary.ran$region.un$mean[61]) * 1.603481

PS.: the fitted (Intercept) is -0.9055 (you have missed the zero)

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problems with prediction of a spatial model
parts:
On 11/08/15 12:59, Finn Lindgren wrote:
> Since E( exp(X) ) > exp( E(X) ), just taking the transformation of the
> posterior mean of the linear predictor does not give the posterior
> mean of the transformed prediction.

This point can be empirically addressed by the following example

n <- 100
e <- runif(n, 1, 10)
x <- runif(n)
require(INLA)

b0 <- seq(-2,2,length=31)
stat <- bias <- rep(NA, length(b0))

for (k in 1:length(b0)) {
y <- rpois(n, exp(b0[k]+x)*e)
stat[k] <- mean(y)
r <- inla(y~x, 'poisson', data=list(y=y,e=e,x=x), E=e,
control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))
e.mean <- exp(r$summary.fix[1,1]+r$summary.fix[2,1]*x)
mean.e <- r$summary.fitted.val$mean
bias[k] <- mean(e.mean/mean.e)
}

plot(b0, bias) ### or plot(stat, bias)

This figure shows that the bias is higher for smaller counts.

Elias

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problems with prediction of a spatial model
parts:
I think that the offset/Exposure is missed in the inla formula/call.
There are three ways to do it in INLA (
http://www.math.ntnu.no/~eliask/br2015/r/offset_example.R ) and in one
of such ways you have to account for it in the linear.predictor output
afterwords.
